name: TurkeyBranch
title: Turkey Branch (Montgomery County, Maryland) OpenHydroQual watershed model

readme.summary: Continuous, physically based model of Turkey Branch above USGS gage 01647850 (Turkey Branch near Rockville, Montgomery County, Maryland; 7.1 km²), calibrated by Bayesian inference (MCMC) to USGS flow (WY2022-2025) and stage (WY2024-2025). It has 19 urban hydrologic response units with three soil layers and an unconfined aquifer, open channels with lidar-measured compound sections, streets and storm sewers with inlets and catch basins (dual drainage) for the 11 sub-catchments without a channel, three stormwater ponds, and a gage segment fitted to the continuous USGS record, and is built in OpenHydroQual. This is the model behind the live digital twin, with the parameter set the twin runs (the highest-posterior MCMC sample). Forcing in this package: NOAA AORC hourly precipitation and gridMET reference evapotranspiration, August 2021 to September 2025 (the live twin uses MRMS radar rainfall).
readme.units:
- Time: days since 1899-12-30 00:00 UTC (the spreadsheet serial date; 45931.0 = 2025-10-01 00:00 UTC).
- SI units throughout: lengths and elevations in m (elevations NAVD88), areas in m², flows in m³/day, hydraulic conductivities in m/day, volumes in m³.
- `forcing/precip_scNN.csv`: `t_start,t_end,depth` with the precipitation depth in m over the interval (wet hours only; gaps are zero). `forcing/et_scNN.csv`: `t,rate` daily reference ET in m/day (gridMET ASCE short grass); the model scales it by the crop coefficients.
- `observations/01647850_flow.csv`: `t,flow` in m³/day; `01647850_stage.csv`: `t,depth` in m above the zero-flow gage height of 1.219 m (USGS gage height minus 1.219 m). Hourly in storm events, daily means otherwise.
- The observations use a log-normal error model with first-order autoregressive (AR1) errors; the error standard deviations (s_Q, s_H) and correlation times (t_Q, t_H, days) are parameters of the model.
- Coordinates: the GeoPackage layers are in WGS84 longitude/latitude.
readme.run:
1. Install OpenHydroQual (https://github.com/ArashMassoudieh/OpenHydroQual), a version from October 2026 or later (the model uses the dual-drainage, catch-basin and AR1 observation features).
2. Unzip this package and keep the folder structure (the model file refers to `templates/`, `forcing/` and `observations/` by relative paths). Use the templates supplied here: the model depends on `urban_hru.json`, `compound_channel.json`, `Sewer_system.json`, `dual_drainage.json`, `Stormwater_control_measures.json` and `dam_spillways.json` as included.
3. Open `TurkeyBranch_model.ohq` in the OpenHydroQual GUI and run it, or use the console: `OpenHydroQual-Console TurkeyBranch_model.ohq -w <output folder>`.
4. Outputs go to `output.txt` (all state variables) and `observed_output.txt` (the modelled values at the observation points). With the interpreter the four-year run takes a while; shorten `simulation_end_time` at the top of the model file for a first test.
